## Trial `zram-swap-almalinux9__3HcEWTJ`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All three material outcomes are satisfied with direct, corroborated evidence: 981 MB of zstd-compressed zram swap (well over the 512 MB floor) is active, it is the sole (and thus effectively highest-priority) swap device since no disk-backed swap exists, and boot persistence was directly demonstrated through an actual reboot with boot_id change confirmed both in executor commands and the independent fixed lifecycle snapshots, followed by identical post-reboot swap state. Operational hygiene is clean apart from a trivial leftover /tmp/reboot.log.

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **min-512mb-compressed-swap — Satisfied:** At least 512 MB of compressed in-memory (zram) swap is active on node1
  - **Why:** zram-generator configured zram0 at 981 MB with zstd compression, well above the 512 MB minimum. swapon --show and zramctl confirm the device active both immediately after setup and after a full reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ef4ad05f2f404764`, `cmd-a031977044894d1f`
- **preferred-over-disk-swap — Satisfied:** zram swap is preferred over any disk-backed swap
  - **Why:** zram0 was configured with swap-priority=100. Baseline showed zero pre-existing disk swap devices (empty /proc/swaps), and post-configuration/post-reboot swapon --show lists only zram0 with no competing disk-backed entries, so the priority ordering is moot but consistent with the requirement.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-f6b9a59754544d01`, `cmd-ef4ad05f2f404764`, `cmd-a031977044894d1f`
- **active-at-boot — Satisfied:** zram swap is active at boot (persists across restarts)
  - **Why:** A generator-based static unit (dev-zram0.swap / systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service) was installed via /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf. The executor captured a genuine pre-restart baseline (boot_id d6298ced..., 981M zram active), issued a real reboot, observed the boot_id change to 1c856cb8... with uptime reset to 0, and confirmed post-reboot that swapon/zramctl again show the identical 981M zstd zram0 swap active at priority 100 with no manual intervention. This transition is independently corroborated by the fixed global before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots, which show the same boot_id change.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-b39e1d15adc546a2`, `cmd-ef7145d7dc6d4328`, `cmd-022c9e032b4f493b`, `cmd-a031977044894d1f`, `cmd-d94d66dd53df48f7`
